title: How much does the output change?
subtitle: Linear functions · 3 official questions

sections.heading: Where this sits for you
body: **3 of the official questions in Linear functions are this one** — 0 Easy, 0 Medium, 3 Hard.
It is top-heavy: most versions are Hard, so it only earns study time once your target actually requires that tier.

sections.heading: How to spot it
body: You are looking at this pattern when:
- The question asks 'by how much' the output increases or decreases when the input increases by some amount, or asks for the change over an interval on a graph.
- It doesn't ask for the output at a single point.

sections.heading: The method
body: - 1) Change in output = slope × change in input.
- The constant term cancels, so ignore it.
- 2) On a graph, read the y-values at the two ends of the interval and subtract.

sections.heading: Where Desmos fits
body: Evaluate f(a + h) − f(a) for any convenient a to confirm.
For a pictured graph, reading two points by hand is faster.

sections.heading: What it is built to catch
body: You plug the change amount straight into the function and include the intercept.
Or on a graph you report the output at the end of the interval instead of the difference between the two ends.

sections.heading: You are losing these
body: Before you choose, say out loud what the question is asking for — not what you solved for.
